```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(lubridate)
source("../../R/portal_config.R")
cfg <- portal_cfg
rel <- portal_release
labs <- portal_labels
v2_current <- rel$is_current(cfg)
version <- cfg$previous_release
start_date <- as.Date(cfg$coverage$start)
end_date <- as.Date(cfg$coverage$end)
base_url <- "https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002"

# The download scripts are kept as text files beside this page; the dates of
# the release are filled in here.
fill_dates <- function(path) {
  text <- paste(readLines(path, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
  text <- gsub("@FIRST_MONTH@", format(start_date, "%Y%m"), text, fixed = TRUE)
  text <- gsub("@LAST_MONTH@", format(end_date, "%Y%m"), text, fixed = TRUE)
  text <- gsub("@FIRST_DAY_COMPACT@", format(start_date, "%Y%m%d"), text, fixed = TRUE)
  text <- gsub("@LAST_DAY_COMPACT@", format(end_date, "%Y%m%d"), text, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub("@FIRST_DAY@", rel$day_text(start_date), text, fixed = TRUE)
}
```

What changed in release `r cfg$release` since release `r cfg$previous_release`,
and a table to move code from the old files and names to the new ones. The
page ends with the [Release v0.0.2](#release-v002) section: its files for
download, and how it was computed.

```{r status}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
if (v2_current) {
  cat("Release ", cfg$release, " is the current release. It covers the days ",
      rel$coverage_text(cfg), ". Release ", cfg$previous_release,
      " stays available but is no longer extended.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("Release ", cfg$release, " is the upcoming release; its files are being produced. ",
      "Until they are available, release ", cfg$current_release, " is the one to use. ",
      "It covers ", portal_labels$month_range(cfg$coverage$start, cfg$coverage$end),
      " and will not be extended.\n", sep = "")
}
```

A **release** is a set of files produced by one version of the OPDI software,
with one set of names and meanings. Every row says which release it belongs
to, in its column `release`. Older releases are on the [Roadmap](../roadmap.qmd#past-releases).

## What is new in release v2.0.0

### One file per day, and events with their measurements

Release v2.0.0 has two files per day:

- the **flight list**, one row per flight, and
- the **flight events**, one row per event, with the event's measurements as
  columns, and the columns of its flight.

A measurement no longer needs a join to its event, and an event no longer
needs a join to its flight. The separate measurements files are no longer
produced. A day's files hold the flights first seen that day,
with all their events, also those after midnight (see
[Data](index.qmd#which-day-a-flight-belongs-to)).

### Worldwide coverage

Release v2.0.0 covers every flight the OpenSky Network received, anywhere in
the world.

### More event types

Release v2.0.0 adds these event families, all listed on the
[Data dictionary](dictionary.qmd#event-types).

- **Runway milestones**: start of the take-off roll, take-off (`ATOT`),
  passage over the runway threshold (`xing-runway-threshold`), touchdown
  (`ALDT`), line-up, runway vacated, runway crossings and go-arounds.
- **Block times**: off-block (`AOBT`) and in-block (`AIBT`), when the aircraft
  leaves and reaches its parking position.
- **Distance rings**: crossings of circles of 40 to 120 NM around the
  departure and destination airports.
- **Level-offs**: periods of level flight during the climb and the descent.
- **Holding**: start and end of each holding pattern, with its duration,
  distance and number of loops.
- **Point merge**: the legs of point merge arrival procedures, with their time
  and distance.
- **FIR crossings**: each passage from one flight information region to the
  next.

### A richer flight list

The flight list holds the main times of each flight, copied from its events:
take-off and landing, off-block and in-block, the runways and stands used and
the times of crossing the distance rings. It also says how each airport was decided
(`adep_source`, `ades_source`) and whether a row counts as a departure or an
arrival (`movement_dep`, `movement_arr`). Column names are in lower case.

### One flight across a reception gap

When an aircraft is out of range of every receiver for more than 30 minutes,
for example over an ocean, release v0.0.2 started a new flight after the gap.
Release v2.0.0 keeps one flight when the data on both sides fit one continuous
flight (see [Track identity](../algorithms/tracks.qmd)). Long flights are
therefore more often one row, with both airports.

### Other changes

- **Cleaner positions**: repeated, impossible and isolated values are removed
  before any event is detected (see
  [Trajectory cleaning](../algorithms/cleaning.qmd)).
- **Documented and checked methods**: each has a page in
  [OPDI Algorithms](../algorithms/index.qmd) on how it works, what it was compared
  with, how accurate it is and where it fails.
  [Data quality](../accuracy/index.qmd) gives how often every
  item exists and how close it is to the records, overall and per airport.
- **Trino**: the files can be queried with SQL on the OpenSky Network's Trino
  instance, without downloading them (see [Data Access](access.qmd)).

## Changes in meaning

These names stay, but their meaning or method changed. Check code that uses
them.

| Name | In release v0.0.2 | In release v2.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `top-of-climb`, `top-of-descent` | The start and end of the cruise, from flight phases. | The method of EUROCONTROL's vertical flight efficiency indicators (see [Vertical events](../algorithms/tops.qmd)). |
| `flight_id` (`ID`) | Built from the address, the call sign and the month. | Built from the address and the time of the first position (see [Dictionary](dictionary.qmd#identifiers)). The identifiers of the two releases do not match. |
| `adep`, `ades` | Nearest airport within 30 NM, from positions below 4,000 ft. | A new method that can also leave an airport undecided (see [Departure and destination airports](../algorithms/airports.qmd)). |

## Moving from v0.0.2 {#moving-from-v0.0.2}

Each file, column or event type of release v0.0.2, and what replaces it in
release v2.0.0.

| Release v0.0.2 | Release v2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `flight_list/flight_list_YYYYMM.parquet`, one file per month | `flight_list/flight_list_YYYYMMDD.parquet`, one file per day |
| `flight_events/flight_events_YYYYMMDD_YYYYMMDD.parquet`, one file per ten days | `flight_events/flight_events_YYYYMMDD.parquet`, one file per day |
| `measurements/measurements_YYYYMMDD_YYYYMMDD.parquet`, one file per ten days | No file. The measurements are columns of the flight events file. |
| Flight list `ID` | `flight_id` |
| Flight list `ICAO24`, `FLT_ID`, `DOF`, `ADEP`, `ADES`, `ADEP_P`, `ADES_P`, `REGISTRATION`, `MODEL`, `TYPECODE`, `ICAO_AIRCRAFT_CLASS`, `ICAO_OPERATOR`, `FIRST_SEEN`, `LAST_SEEN`, `VERSION` | The same names in lower case: `icao24`, `flt_id`, `dof`, and so on |
| Events `id` | `event_id` |
| Events `altitude` (feet) | `altitude_ft` (feet) |
| Events `flight_id`, `type`, `event_time`, `longitude`, `latitude`, `source`, `version`, `info` | The same names |
| Measurements with `type` = `Distance flown (NM)` | Column `distance_flown_nm` |
| Measurements with `type` = `Time Passed (s)` | Column `time_passed_s` |
| Measurements `id`, `event_id`, `value`, `version` | Rebuilt by the `measurements` view: `id` is the `event_id` followed by `_d` (distance) or `_t` (time) |
| Event `take-off` | `ATOT` |
| Event `landing` (first position on the ground) | `ALDT` (touchdown). Release v2.0.0 has no event `landing`. Its new event `xing-runway-threshold` is the passage over the runway threshold, a few seconds before touchdown. |
| Events `first-xing-fl{level}` and `last-xing-fl{level}` | `xing-fl{level}` for every crossing. The first crossing has `crossing_seq` 1 in `info`; the last has the highest `crossing_seq` of that level on the flight. `direction` in `info` says `up` or `down`. |
| Events `entry-runway` and `exit-runway` | `line-up`, `runway-vacated`, `runway-crossing-entry` and `runway-crossing-vacated`, which say what the aircraft did on the runway |
| Events `entry-taxiway`, `exit-taxiway`, `entry-parking_position`, `exit-parking_position` | The same names |
| Area covered: a box around Europe | The whole world. To keep the old area, filter on the airports or on the event positions. |

### Getting the old shapes

Views give the data the shape of release v0.0.2, for code written for it.
They have the same names in Trino and in DuckDB.

| Old shape | Trino and DuckDB view | Python reader |
|---|---|---|
| Flight list (lower-case names and order of v0.0.2, 16 columns) | `flight_list_v0` | `published.as_flight_list_v0(flights)` |
| Flight events (without measurements) | `events` | `published.as_events(events)` |
| Measurements (one row per value) | `measurements` | `published.as_measurements(events)` |

[Data Access](access.qmd) shows how to use them. The views change the shape, not
the content: rows follow the methods of release v2.0.0. Identifiers are text
and do not match the 64-bit integer identifiers of release v0.0.2, so rows
cannot be joined to v0.0.2 files by identifier. The column `version` holds the
version of each method, not "v0.0.2". In the `measurements` view every event
has one row for the distance flown and one for the time passed, even when the
value is empty, as in release v0.0.2; other measurement types have a row only
when they have a value. The old flight list view leaves out the columns that
release v0.0.2 did not have.

## Release v0.0.2 {#release-v002}

```{r status-v002}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
if (v2_current) {
  cat("::: {.callout-note appearance=\"simple\"}\n",
      "Release ", version, " is the **previous** release. ",
      "For new work, use release ", cfg$release, ": see [Data](index.qmd) and ",
      "[Moving from v0.0.2](#moving-from-v0.0.2), which explains how to move code from ",
      "one to the other.\n:::\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("::: {.callout-note appearance=\"simple\"}\n",
      "Release ", version, " is the release available today. Release ", cfg$release,
      ", described in the rest of OPDI Data, is being produced and will replace it. ",
      "[Moving from v0.0.2](#moving-from-v0.0.2) explains what changes.\n:::\n", sep = "")
}
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Coverage:** `r labs$month_range(start_date, end_date)`, a box around Europe | **Last refresh:** `r cfg$refresh_label` | **Version:** `r version`
:::

### What release v0.0.2 contains

Release `r version` has three tables, each split into files of several days:

| Table | One row per | One file per | Download |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flight list | flight | month | [Flight list files](#flight-list-files) |
| Flight events | event | ten days | [Flight events files](#flight-events-files) |
| Measurements | measured value | ten days | [Measurements files](#measurements-files) |

Two tables of open reference data, used to name airports and runways, can be
downloaded from [OurAirports](https://ourairports.com/):
[airports (CSV)](https://davidmegginson.github.io/ourairports-data/airports.csv)
and [runways (CSV)](https://davidmegginson.github.io/ourairports-data/runways.csv).

The files are in Parquet, a column-based file format that most data tools
read. A ten-day file is named after its first day and the day after its last
day: `flight_events_20220101_20220111.parquet` holds 1 to 10 January 2022.

#### How the tables relate


- **Flight list**: for each flight, the aircraft address (`ICAO24`), call sign
  (`FLT_ID`), date of flight (`DOF`), departure and destination airports
  (`ADEP`, `ADES`), other possible airports (`ADEP_P`, `ADES_P`), data on the
  aircraft and the first and last time it was seen.
- **Event**: a moment in a flight, with a time, a position and an altitude in
  feet. `flight_id` links it to the flight list's `ID`.
- **Measurement**: a value attached to an event, the distance flown
  (`type` = `Distance flown (NM)`) or the time passed (`type` =
  `Time Passed (s)`) since the start of the flight. `event_id` links it to the
  event's `id`.
- The airport and runway tables are a selection of the OurAirports columns.

The position reports of a flight can be fetched from the OpenSky Network's
historical database with `ICAO24`, the call sign and the time from
`FIRST_SEEN` to `LAST_SEEN`, for example with the tools on its
[data tools page](https://opensky-network.org/data/data-tools).

### Download scripts

Each file has its own web address:

```
https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002/flight_list/flight_list_{YYYYMM}.parquet
https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002/flight_events/flight_events_{YYYYMMDD}_{YYYYMMDD}.parquet
https://www.eurocontrol.int/performance/data/download/OPDI/v002/measurements/measurements_{YYYYMMDD}_{YYYYMMDD}.parquet
```

`YYYYMM` is the year and month. In the ten-day files, the first date is the
first day of the period and the second the day after its last day. Periods
start on `r rel$day_text(start_date)` and follow each other every ten days.

The scripts download every file of the release into a folder `data/`. Change
the dates in `periods` to download less.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}

### Flight list files {#flight-list-files}

One file per month, from `r format(start_date, "%B %Y")` to
`r format(end_date, "%B %Y")`.

```{r flight-list-files}
#| echo: false
flight_list_entries <- local({
  entries <- c()
  current <- floor_date(start_date, "month")
  while (current <= end_date) {
    name <- paste0("flight_list_", format(current, "%Y%m"), ".parquet")
    entries <- c(entries, paste0(
      "- **", format(current, "%B %Y"), "**: [", name, "](", base_url, "/flight_list/", name, ")"
    ))
    current <- current %m+% months(1)
  }
  paste(entries, collapse = "\n")
})
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}

## Show the flight list files

`r flight_list_entries`

:::

### Flight events files {#flight-events-files}

One file per ten days, from `r rel$day_text(start_date)`.

```{r ten-day-entries}
#| echo: false
ten_day_entries <- function(table) {
  entries <- c()
  current <- start_date
  while (current < end_date) {
    following <- current + 10
    name <- paste0(table, "_", format(current, "%Y%m%d"), "_", format(following, "%Y%m%d"), ".parquet")
    entries <- c(entries, paste0(
      "- **", rel$day_text(current), " to ", rel$day_text(following - 1), "**: [",
      name, "](", base_url, "/", table, "/", name, ")"
    ))
    current <- following
  }
  paste(entries, collapse = "\n")
}
flight_events_entries <- ten_day_entries("flight_events")
measurements_entries <- ten_day_entries("measurements")
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse="true"}

## Show the flight events files

`r flight_events_entries`

:::

### Measurements files {#measurements-files}

One file per ten days, over the same periods as the flight events.

### How release v0.0.2 was computed

An earlier version of the OPDI software produced release `r version`. Its
methods differ from those in [OPDI Algorithms](../algorithms/index.qmd), which
apply to release `r cfg$release`.

#### Flights and their identifiers

The position reports of the OpenSky Network (state vectors) were grouped by
aircraft address (`icao24`) and call sign. A group was split into separate
flights where two consecutive reports were more than 30 minutes apart, or
more than 10 minutes apart while the aircraft was below 1 km. Each flight got
an identifier made of the SHA-256 hash of the address and call sign, a
sequence number, and the year and month.

#### Departure and destination airports

A circle of 30 NM radius around every airport was filled with H3 cells of
resolution 7. H3 divides the Earth into hexagonal cells; these cover about
5 km² each. Only reports below 4,000 ft were kept, and each was matched to the
airports whose circle contains its cell. The airport nearest to the first (or
last) matching report became the departure (or destination) airport; the other
candidates went into `ADEP_P` (or `ADES_P`).

#### Flight events

| Event type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `level-start`, `level-end` | Start and end of a level segment. |
| `top-of-climb` | First report of the first cruise phase. |
| `top-of-descent` | Last report of the last cruise phase. |
| `take-off` | First report of the climb phase after a ground phase. |
| `landing` | First report of the ground phase after a descent phase. |
| `first-xing-fl50`, `first-xing-fl70`, `first-xing-fl100`, `first-xing-fl245` | First crossing of flight level 50, 70, 100 or 245. |
| `last-xing-fl50`, `last-xing-fl70`, `last-xing-fl100`, `last-xing-fl245` | Last crossing of that flight level. |
| `entry-runway`, `exit-runway` | Entry into and exit from a runway. |
| `entry-taxiway`, `exit-taxiway` | Entry into and exit from a taxiway. |
| `entry-parking_position`, `exit-parking_position` | Entry into and exit from a parking position (stand). |

The **flight phases** (ground, climb, cruise, level, descent) came from the
fuzzy logic of OpenAP, an open aircraft performance model by Junzi Sun of TU
Delft. For the flight-level crossings, a smoothed flight level was computed
for each report and compared between consecutive reports. Airport areas
(runways, taxiways, parking positions) came from OpenStreetMap, filled with H3
cells of resolution 12, and each report was matched to them. The `info` field
of the airport events holds the OpenStreetMap details of the area, as JSON
text.

#### Measurements

- **Distance flown (NM)**: the great-circle distance between consecutive
  reports, added up from the first report of the flight, in nautical miles.
- **Time Passed (s)**: the time since the first report of the flight, in
  seconds.

Each event got the two values of the report it was taken from.
